old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Xoossi ba medhdhidobaa ubbaa be7is; be7ishin, keehippe lo77o.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ጦኦስሲ በ ሜꬍꬊዶበአ ኡብበአ ቤዒስ፤ ቤዒሺን፣ ኬእሂፕፔ ሎዕዖ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: እግዚአብሔርም ያደረገውን ሁሉ አየ፥ እነሆም፥ እጅግ መልካም ነበረ።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good.

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Goday Abraama, "Ne biittaappe, ne dabbotaappenne ne aawaa keettaappe kiyada taani nena bessana biittaa ba" giis.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ጎደይ አብረአመ፣ "ኔ ቢኢትተአፕፔ፣ ኔ ደብቦተአፕፔንኔ ኔ አአወአ ኬእትተአፕፔ ኪየደ ተአኒ ኔነ ቤስሰነ ቢኢትተአ በ" ጊኢስ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: እግዚአብሔርም አብራምን አለው፦ ከአገርህ ከዘመዶችህም ከአባትህም ቤት ተለይተህ እኔ ወደማሳይህ ምድር ውጣ።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: Now the LORD said to Abram, "Leave your country, and your relatives, and your father's house, and go to the land that I will show you."

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Taani nena gita dere oothana; nena anjjana; ne sunthaakkaXoqqissana; neeni anjjo gidana.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ተአኒ ኔነ ጊተ ዴሬ ኦኦꬃነ፤ ኔነ አንጅጀነ፤ ኔ ሱንꬃአክከጦቅቂስሰነ፤ ኔእኒ አንጅጆ ጊደነ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: ታላቅ ሕዝብም አደርግሃለሁ፥ እባርክሃለሁም፥ ስምህንም አከብራለሁ፤ ለበረከትም ሁን።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great. You will be a blessing.

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Xoossi Muuse, "TAANI DE7IYAAGAA" giis.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ጦኦስሲ ሙኡሴ፣ "ተአኒ ዴዒየአገአ" ጊኢስ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: እግዚአብሔርም ሙሴን፦ እኔ ያለሁና የምኖር ነኝ አለው።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: God said to Moses, "I AM WHO I AM."

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Xoossi ha qaalata ubbaa haasayidi hagaadaa giis:
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ጦኦስሲ ሀ ቀአለተ ኡብበአ ሀአሰዪዲ ሀገአደአ ጊኢስ፦
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: እግዚአብሔርም እነዚህን ቃሎች ሁሉ ተናገረ እንዲህም አለ፦
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: God spoke all these words, saying:

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Taani nena Gibxxe biittaappe, aylletethaa keettaappe kessida Godaa ne Xoossaa.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ተአኒ ኔነ ጊብጥጤ ቢኢትተአፕፔ፣ አይልሌቴꬃአ ኬእትተአፕፔ ኬስሲደ ጎደአ ኔ ጦኦስሰአ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: ከግብፅ ምድር ከባርነት ቤት ያወጣሁህ እግዚአብሔር አምላክህ እኔ ነኝ።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Goday ne Xoossay nees immiya biittan ne laythay adussana mela, ne aawaanne ne aayee bonchcha.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ጎደይ ኔ ጦኦስሰይ ኔእስ ኢምሚየ ቢኢትተን ኔ ለይꬃይ አዱስሰነ ሜለ፣ ኔ አአወአንኔ ኔ አአዬእ ቦንችቻ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: እግዚአብሔር አምላክህ በሚሰጥህ ምድር ዕድሜህ እንዲረዝም አባትህንና እናትህን አክብር።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the LORD your God gives you.

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Isra7eelee, siya! Goday nu Xoossay issi Godaa.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ኢስረዔእሌእ፣ ሲየ! ጎደይ ኑ ጦኦስሰይ ኢስሲ ጎደአ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: እስራኤል ሆይ፥ ስማ፤ አምላካችን እግዚአብሔር አንድ እግዚአብሔር ነው።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: Hear, Israel: the LORD is our God; the LORD is one.

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Godaanne ne Xoossaa ne kumetha wozanaappe, ne kumetha shemppuwaappenne ne kumetha wolqqaappe siiqa.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ጎደአንኔ ኔ ጦኦስሰአ ኔ ኩሜꬃ ዎዘነአፕፔ፣ ኔ ኩሜꬃ ሼምፕፑወአፕፔንኔ ኔ ኩሜꬃ ዎልቅቀአፕፔ ሲኢቀ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: አንተም አምላክህን እግዚአብሔርን በፍጹም ልብህ በፍጹምም ነፍስህ በፍጹምም ኃይልህ ውደድ።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Taani nena azazabiikkinaa? Minna, xala; yayyoppa, dagammoppa; ayssi giikko, neeni biyaaso ubban Goday ne Xoossay neera de7ees.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ተአኒ ኔነ አዘዘቢኢክኪነአ? ሚንነ፣ ጠለ፤ የይዮፕፐ፣ ደገምሞፕፐ፤ አይስሲ ጊኢክኮ፣ ኔእኒ ቢየአሶ ኡብበን ጎደይ ኔ ጦኦስሰይ ኔእረ ዴዔእስ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: እነሆ፥ አዘዝሁህ፤ ጽና፥ አይዞህ፤ አትፍራ፥ አትደንግጥ፤ አምላክህ እግዚአብሔር በምትሄድበት ሁሉ ከአንተ ጋር ነውና።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: Haven't I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don't be afraid. Don't be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Asay bolla bagga xeellees, shin Goday wozanaa xeellees.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: አሰይ ቦልለ በግገ ጤእልሌእስ፣ ሺን ጎደይ ዎዘነአ ጤእልሌእስ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: ሰው ፊትን ያያል፥ እግዚአብሔር ግን ልብን ያያል።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: For man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Taani ta Wozanchchay de7eyssa erais; wurssethanikka i sa7aa bollan eqqana.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ተአኒ ተ ዎዘንችቻይ ዴዔይስሰ እረኢስ፤ ዉርስሴꬃኒክከ ኢ ሰዓአ ቦልለን እቅቀነ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: እኔ ግን ወዳጄ ሕያው እንደ ሆነ፥ በመጨረሻም ዘመን በምድር ላይ እንደሚቆም አውቃለሁ።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth.

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Iita asata zoriyaa kaallonna, nagaraanchchata ogiyan eqqonna, qilliicciyaageeta uttethaan uttonna uray anjjettidaagaa.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ኢኢተ አሰተ ዞሪየአ ከአልሎንነ፣ ነገረአንችቻተ ኦጊየን እቅቆንነ፣ ቂልሊኢጭጪየአጌእተ ኡትቴꬃአን ኡትቶንነ ኡረይ አንጅጄትቲደአገአ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: ምክርን በክፉዎች ያልሄደ፥ በኃጢአተኞችም መንገድ ያልቆመ፥ በዋዘኞችም ወንበር ያልተቀመጠ ሰው ምስጉን ነው።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: Blessed is the man who doesn't walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers.

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Shin iya ufayssay Godaa wogaa bollan de7ees; gallassanne qamma iya wogaa qoppees.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ሺን ኢየ ኡፈይስሰይ ጎደአ ዎገአ ቦልለን ዴዔእስ፤ ገልለስሰንኔ ቀምመ ኢየ ዎገአ ቆፕፔእስ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: ነገር ግን በእግዚአብሔር ሕግ ደስ ይለዋል፥ ሕጉንም በቀንና በሌሊት ያሰላስላል።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: But his delight is in the LORD's law. On his law he meditates day and night.

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Goday tana heemmiyaagaa; taw aynne paccenna.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ጎደይ ተነ ሄእምሚየአገአ፤ ተው አይንኔ ፐጭጬንነ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: እግዚአብሔር እረኛዬ ነው፥ የሚያሳጣኝም የለም።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: The LORD is my shepherd: I shall lack nothing.

old_testament_seed_verses.gof_latin: Irxxa maataa bollan tana zin77issees; shemppissiya haathaakko tana kaallees.
old_testament_seed_verses.gof_fidel: ኢርጥጠ መአተአ ቦልለን ተነ ዚንዕዒስሴእስ፤ ሼምፕፒስሲየ ሀአꬃአክኮ ተነ ከአልሌእስ።
old_testament_seed_verses.amh_fidel: በለመለመ መስክ ያሳድረኛል፤ በዕረፍት ውኃ ዘንድ ይመራኛል።
old_testament_seed_verses.eng_web: He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.

oral_literature.english_meaning: Something inevitable / unavoidable cultural duty (Gofatho explanation: bare, attonnabaa)
Grew old without growing tall / stunted growth (Gofatho explanation: Ceeggis, diccenna)
Multiplied, gave birth, reproduced abundantly (Gofatho explanation: yelettis, daris)
Caught someone's eye / was envied or bewitched by evil eye (Gofatho explanation: bitettis)
Fills the eye / looks impressive and pleasing (Gofatho explanation: Teematees, oyyanttees)
Food and drink nourished the body well (Gofatho explanation: mida uyidabay ashos giigis)
Knocked to the ground / defeated or ruined (Gofatho explanation: baayisis, wadhdhis)
Passed away / died (literally: the earth wore/hid them) (Gofatho explanation: hayqqis)
Shocked the whole land / caused an uproar (Gofatho explanation: dere daganthis)
Fell into extreme poverty (Gofatho explanation: manqqis)
Sweet-natured, charming, pleasant person (lit. sweet saliva) (Gofatho explanation: mala lo7o)
Reckless or taboo transgression (Gofatho explanation: zambbo pala)
Harmonious, comfortable for living together (Gofatho explanation: duussas injje)
Eloquent or sharp-tongued speaker (Gofatho explanation: dooni pgoppo)
The assembly place became empty / loss of wise elders (Gofatho explanation: wogiaa asi dhayis)
Died prematurely before reaching maturity (Gofatho explanation: dicci simmonna hayqqis)
Startled / terrified someone (Gofatho explanation: daganthis)
Time is running out / deadline approached (Gofatho explanation: wodey matis)
Begged / pleaded humbly (lit. held the foot) (Gofatho explanation: Woossis)
Peaceful reconciliation and harmony (Gofatho explanation: siga)
Malicious plot or curse (Gofatho explanation: iita pala)
Starts working diligently (Gofatho explanation: ooso achchees, ooso oykkees)
Cornered / pressured someone relentlessly (lit. stood them on one foot) (Gofatho explanation: un77ethis)
Cold and wet (lit. a dog's nose) (Gofatho explanation: irxxa)
Easy and agreeable (lit. taro with milk) (Gofatho explanation: injje)
Scattered in disorder (Gofatho explanation: dharccettis, maara dhayis)
Distant, foreign, or hostile land (Gofatho explanation: haaho, allaga gade)
Goodness blossoms from its young shoot (good character shows early).
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 40

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Lo77oy wadhdhin sakkenna; lomppi qoommin qum7enna.
oral_literature.english_meaning: What is good does not hurt when it falls, nor spoil when stored.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 40

oral_literature.english_meaning: Beneath a good appearance, there can be hidden flaws.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 40

oral_literature.english_meaning: Outwardly pleasant, but inwardly sharp/difficult.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 40

oral_literature.english_meaning: Even a difficult person/thing saves you in a time of crisis.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 40

oral_literature.english_meaning: There is no such thing as bad water or a bad mother.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 40

oral_literature.english_meaning: Malice ruins relationships just as mud stains.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 40

oral_literature.english_meaning: Evil deeds disturb one's sleep.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 40

oral_literature.english_meaning: An unwelcome guest stays for seven nights.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 40

oral_literature.english_meaning: Taking shelter from the rain only to end up in a downpour.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 41

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Care wozanan yedhdhin oqane uloy sakkees.
oral_literature.english_meaning: Stepping on a thorn in the heart causes the stomach to ache (hidden resentment).
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 41

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Yessi be7i yeekkees; missi be7i bookkees.
oral_literature.english_meaning: Crying simply because others cry; digging because others dig (blind imitation).
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 41

oral_literature.english_meaning: In the stampede of horses, the donkey gets trampled (collateral damage).
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 42

oral_literature.english_meaning: A child who will grow strong grows by stumbling and learning.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 42

oral_literature.english_meaning: If hung up close by, won't the dog take it? (temptation left within reach).
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 42

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Godaa ammanida dorssiyaa goynaa karen ayssawus.
oral_literature.english_meaning: The sheep that trusts its master leaves its fat tail outside the door.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ጌታዋን የተማመነች በግ ላቷን ውጭ ታሳድራለች።
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 42

oral_literature.english_meaning: Excessive haste leads to delay (haste makes waste).
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 42

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Kayso kushe qanxxin doore bolla wodhdhees.
oral_literature.english_meaning: When a thief's hand is cut, it falls on the heap.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: የሌባ እጅ ቢቆረጥ በክምር ላይ ይወድቃል።
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 42

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Yelanaara giya bin yelisiyaara soon attaawus.
oral_literature.english_meaning: The woman in labor went to the market while the midwife stayed home.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: አራሷ ገበያ ስትሄድ አዋላጇ ቤት ቀረች።
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 42

oral_literature.english_meaning: What goes beyond human reach is eaten by vultures.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 42

oral_literature.english_meaning: A knife of betrayal breaks inside the liver.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 42

oral_literature.english_meaning: To strike standing up, one first crouches low (strategic preparation).
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 42

oral_literature.english_meaning: Do not grab a leopard by the tail; if you do, do not let go (finish what you start with resolve).
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 80

oral_literature.english_meaning: The twig that will poke the eye is not seen by the eye.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 8 Textbook, p. 146

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Xeeray duge; dulley pude haniday aybeekko era wodha.
oral_literature.english_meaning: Its tip points down, its base points up — what is it? Answer: A cow's tail.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ጫፉ ወደ ታች፣ መነሻው ወደ ላይ (የላም ጭራ)
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 8 Textbook, p. 34

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Timirtte tamaaribennashin digire tookkis; kushen saatey baawashin saate eriyaba era wodha.
oral_literature.english_meaning: Never went to school yet wears a degree (comb); has no watch on its hand yet knows the time. Answer: A rooster.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ሳይማር ዲግሪ የጫነ፣ ሰዓት ሳይኖረው ሰዓት የሚያውቅ (አውራ ዶሮ)
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 8 Textbook, p. 34

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Gita beshe giddon guutha onggochcho; era wodha.
oral_literature.english_meaning: Inside a large baking pan, a small piece of flatbread. Answer: The tongue (or moon in the sky).
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: በትልቅ ምጣድ ውስጥ ትንሽ እንጎቻ (ምላስ / ጨረቃ)
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 8 Textbook, p. 34

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Dulley tama kayees; xeeray awa kayees; era wodha.
oral_literature.english_meaning: Its bottom warms by the fire; its top warms in the sun. Answer: The center house pole (tuussa).
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ስሩ እሳት ይሞቃል፣ ጫፉ ፀሐይ ይሞቃል (የቤት ምሰሶ)
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 8 Textbook, p. 34

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Gede bishin de7ees; haa yishin de7onaba; era wodha.
oral_literature.english_meaning: It goes forward and never comes back. Answer: Flowing river water.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ወደዚያ ሲሄድ አለ፣ ወደዚህ ሲመጣ የለም (ወንዝ/ውኃ)
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 8 Textbook, p. 34

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Woxxishin woxxees; eqqishin eqqees; uttishin uttiyabaa era wodha.
oral_literature.english_meaning: When you run, it runs; when you stand, it stands; when you sit, it sits. Answer: A shadow.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 8 Textbook, p. 35

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Omarssi pude; wontta duge haniyaba; era wodha.
oral_literature.english_meaning: Goes up in the evening and comes down in the morning. Answer: Door latch / crossbar.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ማታ ወደ ላይ፣ ጠዋት ወደ ታች የሚሆን (የበር መቀርቀሪያ)
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 8 Textbook, p. 35

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Eqqiyade qanthi; uttiyade aduqqiyaba; era wodha.
oral_literature.english_meaning: Short when standing, tall when sitting down. Answer: A dog.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 8 Textbook, p. 35

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Na7iyaa hello guppaws aayiyaa tira harggaws, era wodha.
oral_literature.english_meaning: The daughter jumps up and down while the mother's chest aches. Answer: Pestle and mortar.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ልጅቷ ስትዘል እናትየው ደረቷን ያማታል (ሙቀጫና ዘነዘና)
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 45

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Bollay tama garssay tama giddoy shemppo ashshiyaaba era wodha.
oral_literature.english_meaning: Fire on top, fire underneath, and life-saving food in the middle. Answer: Traditional baked bread (Difo dabbo).
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ላዩ እሳት ታቹ እሳት መሃሉ ነፍስ የሚያድን (ድፎ ዳቦ)
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 45

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Kareetha miiziya bootha marata kaalethawus era wodha.
oral_literature.english_meaning: A black cow leading white calves. Answer: A black clay coffee pot (jebena) surrounded by white coffee cups.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ጥቁር ላም ነጭ ጥጃዎችን ትመራለች (ጀበናና ሲኒዎች)
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 45

oral_literature.response_or_pair: Ne Aawappe durey baawashin dokke ashshenna.
oral_literature.english_meaning: Nothing is straighter than eucalyptus, yet it cannot serve as the center pole -> No one is richer than your father, yet he doesn't spare a calf.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ከባህርዛፍ የቀና የለም ግን ምሰሶ አይሆንም
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 8 Textbook, p. 31-32

oral_literature.english_meaning: Qan77ishe is the friend of Qashe -> The scraping blade is the friend of the hide.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 8 Textbook, p. 32

oral_literature.english_meaning: My ox Shanno strikes the river -> The suitor combs his hair to marry you.
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 46

oral_literature.english_meaning: Chew like dried hide -> Rumble like the ritual drum.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: እንደ ቆዳ ቃሚ -> እንደ ነጋሪት አጉረምርሚ
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 46

oral_literature.english_meaning: Running and running, reach Wolaita -> Ailing and ailing, be left as bones (humorous poetic tease).
oral_literature.source: Gofatho Student Textbook (2015 E.C.), Grade 10 Textbook, p. 47

oral_literature.english_meaning: Death is an inevitable natural duty ('father's tree') for human beings.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ሞት ለሰው ልጅ የማይቀር የአባት ዕዳ (የተፈጥሮ ግዴታ) ነው።

oral_literature.english_meaning: The aroma of traditional beer is better than noisy commotion.

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Qan77ishe 1: Barzaapeppe luuloy baawashin tuussi eqqenna. -> Zaaro: Ne aawappe durey baawashin dokke ashshenna.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ቀንዕዒሼ 1፦ በርዘአፔፕፔ ሉኡሎይ በአወሺን ቱኡስሲ እቅቄንነ። -> ዘአሮ፦ ኔ አአወፕፔ ዱሬይ በአወሺን ዶክኬ አሽሼንነ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Qan77ishe Poetic Duel 1: Nothing is straighter than eucalyptus, yet it cannot stand as a center pole -> No one is richer than your father, yet he never spares a calf.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ቃንጪሼ 1፦ ከባህርዛፍ የቀና የለም ግን ምሰሶ አይቆምም። -> መልስ፦ ከአባትህ የከበረ (ሀብታም) የለም ግን ጥጃ አያሳድግም።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Qan77ishe 2: Qan77ishey qasheko lage -> Zaaro: Qacini harppa lage.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ቀንዕዒሼ 2፦ ቀንዕዒሼይ ቀሼኮ ለጌ -> ዘአሮ፦ ቀጪኒ ሀርፕፐ ለጌ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Qan77ishe Poetic Duel 2: Qan77ishe is the companion of Qashe -> The scraping blade is the companion of the hide.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ቃንጪሼ 2፦ ቃንጪሼ የቃሼ ወዳጅ ነው -> መልስ፦ መፋቂያ ድንጋይ የቆዳ ወዳጅ ነው።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Sedhemenkke 1: Xeeray duge; dulley pude haniday aybeekko era wodha. -> Zaaro: Miiza goyna.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ሴꬌሜንክኬ 1፦ ጤእረይ ዱጌ፤ ዱልሌይ ፑዴ ሀኒደይ አይቤእክኮ እረ ዎꬋ። -> ዘአሮ፦ ሚኢዘ ጎይነ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Sedhemenkke Riddle 1: Its tip points downward and its base points upward — what is it? -> Answer: A cow's tail.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: እንቆቅልሽ 1፦ ጫፉ ወደ ታች፣ መነሻው ወደ ላይ የሆነው ምንድን ነው? -> መልስ፦ የላም ጭራ።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Sedhemenkke 2: Timirtte tamaaribennashin digire tookkis; kushen saatey baawashin saate eriyaba era wodha. -> Zaaro: Awure kutto.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ሴꬌሜንክኬ 2፦ ቲሚርትቴ ተመአሪቤንነሺን ዲጊሬ ቶኦክኪስ፤ ኩሼን ሰአቴይ በአወሺን ሰአቴ እሪየበ እረ ዎꬋ። -> ዘአሮ፦ አዉሬ ኩትቶ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Sedhemenkke Riddle 2: Never went to school yet wears a crown/degree; has no watch on its hand yet knows the time -> Answer: A rooster.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: እንቆቅልሽ 2፦ ትምህርት ሳይማር ዲግሪ የተሸከመ፣ በእጁ ሰዓት ሳይኖረው ሰዓት የሚያውቅ ምንድን ነው? -> መልስ፦ አውራ ዶሮ።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Sedhemenkke 3–10 (pp. 34–35): (1) Gita beshe giddon guutha onggochcho -> Inxxarssa / Agina; (2) Dulley tama kayees, xeeray awa kayees -> Keetha tuussa; (3) Gede bishin de7ees, haa yishin de7onaba -> Shaafa haatha; (4) Woxxishin woxxees, eqqishin eqqees -> Kuya; (8) Omarssi pude, wontta duge -> Pengge sanqa; (10) Eqqiyade qanthi, uttiyade aduqqiyaba -> Kana.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ሴꬌሜንክኬ 3–10 (ፕፕ። 34–35)፦ (1) ጊተ ቤሼ ጊድዶን ጉኡꬃ ኦንግጎችቾ -> ኢንጥጠርስሰ / አጊነ፤ (2) ዱልሌይ ተመ ከዬእስ፣ ጤእረይ አወ ከዬእስ -> ኬእꬃ ቱኡስሰ፤ (3) ጌዴ ቢሺን ዴዔእስ፣ ሀአ ዪሺን ዴዖነበ -> ሻአፈ ሀአꬃ፤ (4) ዎጥጢሺን ዎጥጤእስ፣ እቅቂሺን እቅቄእስ -> ኩየ፤ (8) ኦመርስሲ ፑዴ፣ ዎንትተ ዱጌ -> ፔንግጌ ሰንቀ፤ (10) እቅቂየዴ ቀንꬂ፣ ኡትቲየዴ አዱቅቂየበ -> ከነ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Sedhemenkke Riddles 3–10 (pp. 34–35): (1) Small flatbread in a big pan -> Tongue/Moon; (2) Base warms by fire, top warms in sun -> Center house pole; (3) Goes forward, never returns -> River water; (4) Runs when you run, stands when you stand -> Shadow; (8) Up at night, down in morning -> Door bar; (10) Short standing, tall sitting -> Dog.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: እንቆቅልሽ 3–10 (ገጽ 34–35)፦ (1) በትልቅ ምጣድ ውስጥ ትንሽ እንጎቻ -> ምላስ/ጨረቃ፤ (2) ስሩ እሳት ይሞቃል ጫፉ ፀሐይ ይሞቃል -> የቤት ምሰሶ፤ (3) ሲሄድ አለ ሲመጣ የለም -> የወንዝ ውኃ፤ (4) ስትሮጥ የሚሮጥ ስትቆም የሚቆም -> ጥላ፤ (8) ማታ ወደ ላይ ጠዋት ወደ ታች -> የበር መቀርቀሪያ፤ (10) ሲቆም አጭር ሲቀመጥ ረጅም -> ውሻ።

oral_literature.english_meaning: The man looks straight ahead with alert attention like a horse's ear (idiomatic compound 'para-haythe').
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ሰውየው እንደ ፈረስ ጆሮ ቀጥ ብሎ ወደ ፊት ይመለከታል (በንቃት ያዳምጣል/ይመለከታል)።

oral_literature.english_meaning: His/her life became like a tree standing in floodwater (precarious and troubled).
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: በውኃ ውስጥ እንደቆመ ዛፍ ኑሮው ተናጋ (ተቸገረ)።

oral_literature.english_meaning: He studies holding it in his right hand (with utmost diligence and priority).
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: በቀኝ እጁ ይዞ (በከፍተኛ ትኩረትና ትጋት) ይማራል።

oral_literature.english_meaning: She gritted her teeth (persevered through hardship) and raised him.

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Zine issi doonan cuttidi qachidi oday sa7i wonttishin mana bangga gidis.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ዚኔ ኢስሲ ዶኦነን ጩትቲዲ ቀቺዲ ኦደይ ሰዒ ዎንትቲሺን መነ በንግገ ጊዲስ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: What they agreed upon unanimously yesterday scattered in disorder like spilled barley by morning.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ትናንት በአንድ አፍ ተስማምተው የቋጩት ነገር ሲነጋ እንደ ማና ገብስ ተበታተነ።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Daashshi dhiille baarida asa mela si77i gis.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ደአሽሺ ꬊኢልሌ በአሪደ አሰ ሜለ ሲዕዒ ጊስ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Daashshi stayed completely silent like a person with a mouthful of flour.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ዳሺ ዱቄት እንደጎረሰ ሰው ጭጭ አለ።

oral_literature.english_meaning: Ashshami's heart turned to stone (became unyielding/hard-hearted).

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Tamaarida asi issi gade dichchaas zokko meqethi.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ተመአሪደ አሲ ኢስሲ ገዴ ዲችቻአስ ዞክኮ ሜቄꬂ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: An educated person is the backbone (zokko meqethi) of a nation's development.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: የተማረ ሰው ለአንድ አገር ዕድገት የጀርባ አጥንት ነው።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Ushsha mathoppe maatha mathoy daro iita.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ኡሽሻ መꬆፕፔ መአꬃ መꬆይ ደሮ ኢኢተ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Intoxication from milk (wealth/arrogance) is far worse than intoxication from alcohol.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ከመጠጥ ስካር የወተት (የጥጋብ) ስካር እጅግ ይከፋል።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Ayfe qooqey soo geli aqin wozana qooqey ogen aqis.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: አይፌ ቆኦቄይ ሶኦ ጌሊ አቂን ዎዘነ ቆኦቄይ ኦጌን አቂስ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: While the blind in eye found his way home for the night, the blind in heart spent the night stranded on the road.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ዓይነ ስውር ቤት ገብቶ ሲያድር ልበ ስውር ግን መንገድ ላይ አደረ።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Wodoro miyaara bin bixaala miyaara yasu.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ዎዶሮ ሚየአረ ቢን ቢጠአለ ሚየአረ የሱ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: When the one that chews the rope left, the one that chews the iron bridle arrived (out of the frying pan into the fire).
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ገመድ የምትበላዋ ስትሄድ ልጓም የምትበላዋ መጣች።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Kataman uukettiya soolloy kana inxxarssi aazees.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ከተመን ኡኡኬትቲየ ሶኦልሎይ ከነ ኢንጥጠርስሲ አአዜእስ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: The flatbread baked in the city is as thin as a dog's tongue.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: በከተማ የሚጋገረው እንጀራ እንደ ውሻ ምላስ የሳሳ ነው።

oral_literature.english_meaning: The patient's foot became as cold as a dog's nose.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: የታማሚው እግር እንደ ውሻ አፍንጫ ቀዘቀዘ።

oral_literature.english_meaning: May your mother give birth to you again! (Traditional Gofatho exclamation of admiration and praise).
Became a constant companion ('spouse') of illness.
His body wasted away and became frail from repeated illness.

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Aawa paray wothenna, na7a paray kessenna.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: አአወ ፐረይ ዎꬄንነ፣ ነዓ ፐረይ ኬስሴንነ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: The father's horse does not carry one down, nor the son's horse up (each person must rely on their own effort).
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: የአባት ፈረስ አያወርድም፣ የልጅ ፈረስ አያወጣም።

oral_literature.english_meaning: Passing rain pours as it moves on.
Sitting idle too long consumes the seed grain.
Grain that will satisfy is known right on the grinding stone.
Taking the long, safe road prolongs life.
When the land is quiet, the whole community hears.
Generous inside the house, sharing greens outside.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: በቤት ውስጥ ቸር ሆኖ በውጭ ጎመን ያሳልፋል።

oral_literature.english_meaning: A river about to dry up sweeps away a dog.
A rich person's grave is amidst the flourishing enset garden.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: የሀብታም መቃብር በእንሰት ተክል መካከል ነው።

oral_literature.english_meaning: A cow that refuses to give milk also refuses the grass.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ወተት ልትከለክል ያለች ላም ሣሩንም ትጠላለች።

oral_literature.english_meaning: Weeping when someone is merely tired/ill, only to abandon them when they die.

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Sedhemenkke (p. 39): (1) Gadhi kalo, gezzey kalo, doolloy kosha -> Kazhe (ant/waist); (2) Bukkishin eexees; awishin to7ees -> Wol7anthi (lightning); (3) Ba7iday xugga; tucciday gola -> Badalla (maize cob); (4) Tilil gida dembban issi ayfe atare -> Awa ayfe (the sun).
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ሴꬌሜንክኬ (ፕ። 39)፦ (1) ገꬊ ከሎ፣ ጌዝዜይ ከሎ፣ ዶኦልሎይ ኮሻ -> ከዤ (አንት/ወኢስት)፤ (2) ቡክኪሺን እእጤእስ፤ አዊሺን ቶዔእስ -> ዎልዓንꬂ (ሊግህትኒንግ)፤ (3) በዒደይ ጡግገ፤ ቱጭጪደይ ጎለ -> በደልለ (መኢዜ ጮብ)፤ (4) ቲሊል ጊደ ዴምብበን ኢስሲ አይፌ አተሬ -> አወ አይፌ (ꬄ ሱን)።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Sedhemenkke Riddles (p. 39): (1) Full at bottom and top, thin in the middle -> Ant (Kazhe); (2) Burns when raining, goes out when sunny -> Lightning (Wol7anthi); (3) Maize cob (Badalla); (4) A single pea on a clear plain -> The sun (Awa ayfe).
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: እንቆቅልሾች (ገጽ 39)፦ (1) ቆላው ጥጋብ፣ ደጋው ጥጋብ፣ ወይና ደጋው ረሃብ -> ጉንዳን (Kazhe)፤ (2) ሲዘንብ ይነዳል፣ ፀሐይ ሲወጣ ይጠፋል -> መብረቅ (Wol7anthi)፤ (3) በቆሎ (Badalla)፤ (4) በጠራ ሜዳ ላይ አንዲት አተር -> ፀሐይ (Awa ayfe)።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Saba (Heroic Praise Chants, pp. 45–46): (1) Yeehon shiiqiya saba ('Caliga cokki goyiya sangga godaw...'); (2) Kawo Gaammonaa Amaado Zaala Sabishe ('Haathe oychin maathi immiya, Mari oychin maathi woytiya...'); (3) Arbba naa Tuuthe Bulqqo Sabbishe ('Atare bangga Tophphiyaas gidisiya...').
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ሰበ (ሄሮኢጭ ፕረኢሴ ቻንትስ፣ ፕፕ። 45–46)፦ (1) ዬእሆን ሺኢቂየ ሰበ ('ጨሊገ ጮክኪ ጎዪየ ሰንግገ ጎደው።።።')፤ (2) ከዎ ገአምሞነአ አመአዶ ዘአለ ሰቢሼ ('ሀአꬄ ኦይቺን መአꬂ ኢምሚየ፣ መሪ ኦይቺን መአꬂ ዎይቲየ።።።')፤ (3) አርብበ ነአ ቱኡꬄ ቡልቅቆ ሰብቢሼ ('አተሬ በንግገ ቶጵጪየአስ ጊዲሲየ።።።')።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Saba Heroic Praise Chants (pp. 45–46): (1) Funerary elegy chant; (2) Praise of King Gaammona Amaado Zaala ('Who gives milk when asked for water'); (3) Praise of Tuuthe Bulqqo son of Arbba.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ሙገሳ/ፉከራ (Saba፣ ገጽ 45–46)፦ (1) የለቅሶ ሙገሳ፤ (2) የንጉሥ ጋሞና አማዶ ዛላ ሙገሳ ('ውኃ ሲጠይቁት ወተት የሚሰጥ...')፤ (3) የአርባ ልጅ ቱቴ ቡልቆ ሙገሳ ('አተርና ገብስ ለኢትዮጵያ የሚያበቃ...')።

oral_literature.english_meaning: Too much talk cannot be loaded onto a donkey (concise speech is better than endless chatter).
You ask what you already know, and stumble while looking straight ahead.
Material wealth cannot even step on the heel of education (cannot compare to education).
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ሀብት የትምህርትን ተረከዝ አይረግጥም (ከትምህርት ጋር አይወዳደርም)።

oral_literature.english_meaning: The hen that gathers her grain early in the morning is not snatched by the hawk (early diligence protects one's future).
An elder can even persuade one to swallow dung (the respected authority of elders resolves even the hardest disputes).
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ሽማግሌ ኩስ ያስበላል (የሽማግሌ ምክርና ሽምግልና የማይቻለውን ያስችላል/ያስታርቃል)።

oral_literature.english_meaning: The ceremonial drum is the companion of traditional beer (festive music and hospitality go hand in hand).
One who has studied and traveled surpasses one who has merely aged.
In a community destined to prosper, three people share and drink together in harmony.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: በሚያድግ (በሚበለጽግ) አገር ሦስት ሰው ተጋግዞ ይጠጣል።

oral_literature.english_meaning: The poor person follows by trudging along; the rich person follows after eating.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ድሀ ተጉዞ (ለፍቶ) ይከተላል፤ ሀብታም በልቶ ይከተላል።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Iiti iita wode ashshees; Iiti ishassa; Haatha iitinne aayi iiti baawa.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ኢኢቲ ኢኢተ ዎዴ አሽሼእስ፤ ኢኢቲ ኢሻስሰ፤ ሀአꬃ ኢኢቲንኔ አአዪ ኢኢቲ በአወ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Even something harsh saves you in hard times; there is no bad water or bad mother.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ክፉ ለክፉ ቀን ይደርሳል፤ የውኃ ክፉና የእናት ክፉ የለም።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Iiti iissees, curqqi shaallees; Iitabay zin77i qakkees; Ixxiyaa imathi laappun qamma aqees.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ኢኢቲ ኢኢስሴእስ፣ ጩርቅቂ ሻአልሌእስ፤ ኢኢተበይ ዚንዕዒ ቀክኬእስ፤ ኢጥጢየአ ኢመꬂ ለአፕፑን ቀምመ አቄእስ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Malice ruins relationships as mud stains; evil deeds ruin sleep; an unwelcome guest stays seven nights.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ክፋት ያጋጫል፣ ጭቃ ያቆሽሻል፤ ክፉ ሥራ እንቅልፍ ይነሳል፤ የተጠላ እንግዳ ሰባት ሌሊት ያድራል።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Iras gelidi kaho gishees; Care wozanan yedhdhin oqane uloy sakkees; Yessi be7i yeekkees, missi be7i bookkees.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ኢረስ ጌሊዲ ከሆ ጊሼእስ፤ ጨሬ ዎዘነን ዬꬍꬊን ኦቀኔ ኡሎይ ሰክኬእስ፤ ዬስሲ ቤዒ ዬእክኬእስ፣ ሚስሲ ቤዒ ቦኦክኬእስ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Fleeing rain into a downpour; stepping on a thorn in the heart makes the stomach ache; crying merely because others cry.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ከዝናብ ሸሽቶ ወደ ዶፍ መግባት፤ ቂም በልብ ሲያዝ ውስጡን ያሳምማል፤ ሰው ሲያለቅስ አይቶ ማልቀስ።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Paraa dirguwaan harey hayqqees; Diccana na7i gufanthin diccees; Godaa ammanida dorssiyaa goynaa karen ayssawus; Ellesoy gam7on gathees; Ammano mashshay tiriyaan me7ees; Eqqi caddanaw hokki zuummees.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ፐረአ ዲርጉወአን ሀሬይ ሀይቅቄእስ፤ ዲጭጨነ ነዒ ጉፈንꬂን ዲጭጬእስ፤ ጎደአ አምመኒደ ዶርስሲየአ ጎይነአ ከሬን አይስሰዉስ፤ እልሌሶይ ገምዖን ገꬄእስ፤ አምመኖ መሽሻይ ቲሪየአን ሜዔእስ፤ እቅቂ ጨድደነው ሆክኪ ዙኡምሜእስ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: In the stampede of horses the donkey dies; a growing child grows by stumbling; the sheep that trusts its master leaves its tail outside; haste leads to delay; a knife of betrayal breaks in the liver; to strike standing, one first crouches.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: በፈረሶች ግርግር አህያ ይሞታል፤ የሚያድግ ልጅ እየተደናቀፈ ያድጋል፤ ጌታዋን የተማመነች በግ ላቷን ውጭ ታሳድራለች፤ ችኮላ ወደ መዘግየት ያደርሳል፤ የእምነት ቢላዋ በጉበት ውስጥ ይሰበራል፤ ቆሞ ለመውጋት ጎንበስ ብሎ መጠጋት።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Sedhemenkke (p. 45): (1) Na7iyaa hello guppaws aayiyaa tira harggaws -> Tuutenne udula (pestle & mortar); (2) Bollay tama garssay tama giddoy shemppo ashshiyaaba -> Difo daabbo (baked bread); (3) Kareetha miiziya bootha marata kaalethawus -> Ayfe tukke sinenne zhabana (black coffee pot & white cups).
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ሴꬌሜንክኬ (ፕ። 45)፦ (1) ነዒየአ ሄልሎ ጉፕፐውስ አአዪየአ ቲረ ሀርግገውስ -> ቱኡቴንኔ ኡዱለ (ፔስትሌ & ሞርተር)፤ (2) ቦልለይ ተመ ገርስሰይ ተመ ጊድዶይ ሼምፕፖ አሽሺየአበ -> ዲፎ ደአብቦ (በኬድ ብሬአድ)፤ (3) ከሬእꬃ ሚኢዚየ ቦኦꬃ መረተ ከአሌꬃዉስ -> አይፌ ቱክኬ ሲኔንኔ ዣበነ (ብለጭክ ጮፍፌእ ፖት & ውሂቴ ጩፕስ)።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Riddles (p. 45): (1) Daughter jumps while mother's chest aches -> Pestle and mortar; (2) Fire above, fire below, life-saving food inside -> Baked difo bread; (3) Black cow leading white calves -> Black clay coffee pot and white cups.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: እንቆቅልሾች (ገጽ 45)፦ (1) ልጅቷ ስትዘል እናትየው ደረቷን ያማታል -> ሙቀጫና ዘነዘና፤ (2) ላዩ እሳት ታቹ እሳት መሃሉ ነፍስ የሚያድን -> ድፎ ዳቦ፤ (3) ጥቁር ላም ነጭ ጥጃዎችን ትመራለች -> ጀበናና ሲኒዎች።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Qan77ishe (pp. 46–47): (1) Ta booraa Shannoy shaafi qocees -> Shaaqanchoy nena gelanaw huuphe pixees; (2) Qalqqaaluwada qaamma -> Qaalichaa nagiriitaada guumma; (3) Woxxashe woxxashe wolaythi gakka -> Harggashe harggashe meqethi atta.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ቀንዕዒሼ (ፕፕ። 46–47)፦ (1) ተ ቦኦረአ ሻንኖይ ሻአፊ ቆጬእስ -> ሻአቀንቾይ ኔነ ጌለነው ሁኡጴ ፒጤእስ፤ (2) ቀልቅቀአሉወደ ቀአምመ -> ቀአሊቻአ ነጊሪኢተአደ ጉኡምመ፤ (3) ዎጥጠሼ ዎጥጠሼ ዎለይꬂ ገክከ -> ሀርግገሼ ሀርግገሼ ሜቄꬂ አትተ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Qan77ishe Couplets (pp. 46–47): Traditional rhyming verbal duels.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ቃንጪሼ (ገጽ 46–47)፦ (1) ኮርማዬ ሻኖ ወንዝ ይመታል -> እጮኛሽ አንቺን ለማግባት ፀጉሩን ያበጥራል፤ (2) እንደ ቆዳ ቃሚ -> እንደ ቃልቻ ነጋሪት አጉረምርሚ፤ (3) እየሮጥክ ወላይታ ድረስ -> እየታመምክ አጥንት ቅር።

oral_literature.english_meaning: Whether one likes it or not, an elder's mediation prevails.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: ወደድክም ጠላህም ሽማግሌ ያስታርቃል (የሽማግሌ ቃል አይታጠፍም)።

oral_literature.english_meaning: He who has eaten catches up with the one who has already set out.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: የበላ የሄደውን ይደርሳል (ምግብ የበላ ሰው ብርታት ያገኛል)።

oral_literature.english_meaning: Water devours while smiling (calm appearances can hide danger, like alcohol).
When the stomach is full, even bone marrow tastes bitter.

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Yaare muussi bini qaallis ulo daakkis.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: የአሬ ሙኡስሲ ቢኒ ቀአልሊስ ኡሎ ደአክኪስ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: Greedy overeating tore open Qaallis's stomach even in olden times.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: የስስት (የድግስ) መብል ጥንትም የቃሊስን ሆድ ቀደደ።

oral_literature.gofatho_text: Uttiday dulle pittees, qaaxxiday qanthe pittees.
oral_literature.response_or_pair: ኡትቲደይ ዱልሌ ፒትቴእስ፣ ቀአጥጢደይ ቀንꬄ ፒትቴእስ።
oral_literature.english_meaning: He who sits idle brushes dust off his seat, while he who moves and works prospers.
oral_literature.amharic_meaning: የተቀመጠ መቀመጫውን ያራግፋል፣ የተንቀሳቀሰ (የሠራ) ግን ቅቤ ይቀባል (ይበለጽጋል)።

oral_literature.english_meaning: Scattered in disorder (Gofatho def: dharccettis, maara dhayis)

grammar_rules.morpheme: a, e, i, o, u / aa, ee, ii, oo, uu
grammar_rules.function_gloss: 5 short & 5 long phonemic vowels
grammar_rules.description: Vowel length is phonemic in Gofatho (e.g., tama 'fire' vs. taama 'weak'). High tonal accent is marked on the prominent mora.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: tama ('fire') vs. taama ('weak')

grammar_rules.function_gloss: Glottal stop, 4 ejectives, 1 implosive
grammar_rules.description: In Latin orthography, '7' represents the phonemic glottal stop /ʔ/ (e.g., na7a 'child'), 'dh' is the alveolar implosive /ɗ/, 'x' is /t'/, 'q' is /k'/, 'ph' is /p'/, and 'c' is /tʃ'/.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: na7a [naʔa] ('child'), dhoqqa ('high')

grammar_rules.morpheme: ch [tʃ], sh [ʃ], zh [ʒ], dz [dz], nh [ŋ], ny [ɲ], th [ts/θ]
grammar_rules.function_gloss: Affricates, fricatives, and nasals
grammar_rules.description: Standard Gofatho Latin orthography uses digraphs for palato-alveolar and dental/alveolar sibilants/affricates. Gemination is written by doubling the first letter (e.g., achche, oothis).
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: achche ('tooth'), heedzu ('three'), yeletetha ('birth')
grammar_rules.source: Sellassie Cheru (2015), Table 1, p. 17; Gr. 8-10 Textbooks

grammar_rules.morpheme: th → ꬃ/ꬁ/ꬂ/ꬄ/ꬆ, dh → ꬋ/ꬉ/ꬊ/ꬌ/ꬎ, dz → ꬓ/ꬑ/ꬖ
grammar_rules.function_gloss: Ethiopic Extended-A (U+AB01–U+AB16)
grammar_rules.description: In Gofatho Fidel script (Ooratha Caaquwa C02), dental/alveolar 'th', implosive 'dh', and affricate 'dz' map to Unicode Ethiopic Extended-A characters.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: yeletethaa → ዬሌቴꬃ, dhuman → ꬉማን, heedzu → ሄꬑ

grammar_rules.morpheme: -a, -e, -o (Class I) / -i, -u (Class II)
grammar_rules.function_gloss: Lexical stem terminal vowels (TV)
grammar_rules.description: Every Gofatho noun stem ends in a terminal vowel (-a, -e, -o, -i, -u) that interacts morphophonemically with case, number, and definiteness suffixes.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: kana ('dog'), keethe ('house'), kutho ('hen')

grammar_rules.morpheme: Buzo, Kothe, Shiiqo, Miishe, Beettonabata, Taybettiya/Taybettonna
grammar_rules.function_gloss: Proper, Common, Collective, Material, Abstract, Count/Mass
grammar_rules.description: Grade 8 Qawosa classifies Gofatho nouns into proper (buzo), common (kothe), collective (shiiqo), material (miishe), abstract (beettonabata), countable (taybettiya), and mass (taybettonna).
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: Sawla (Buzo), do7a (Kothe), wude (Shiiqo), siiqo (Beettonabata)

grammar_rules.morpheme: -i / -y (M.SG & PL), -a / -iya (F.SG.DEF)
grammar_rules.function_gloss: NOM (Subject Case / Yohaadde)
grammar_rules.description: Marks the grammatical subject (yohaadde) of a clause. Masculine and plural nouns take -i/-y; definite feminine nouns take -(i)ya.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: meddaawa-i soo-n d-es ('The groom is at home')

grammar_rules.morpheme: -a / -aa (M.DEF), -o / -iyo (F.DEF)
grammar_rules.function_gloss: ACC / ABS (Direct Object / Kaalodde)
grammar_rules.description: Marks the direct object (kaalodde) and serves as the oblique base for peripheral case suffixes.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: boora-a shukk-is ('He slaughtered the ox')

grammar_rules.morpheme: -s / -si / -w / -u
grammar_rules.function_gloss: DAT ('to / for')
grammar_rules.description: Attaches to the accusative/genitive stem to mark recipient, beneficiary, or purpose.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: Yoosefa-s ('to Joseph'), asa ubbaa-s ('for all people')

grammar_rules.morpheme: -n / -ni
grammar_rules.function_gloss: LOC / INST ('in, at, on, by, with')
grammar_rules.description: Marks spatial/temporal location as well as instrument or manner.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: Galiila-n ('in Galilee'), toora-n caddidi ('stabbing with a spear')

grammar_rules.morpheme: -ppe / -fe
grammar_rules.function_gloss: ABL ('from, out of, than')
grammar_rules.description: Marks source of motion, origin, or standard of comparison.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: Galiila-ppe Yerusalaame ('from Galilee to Jerusalem')

grammar_rules.morpheme: -ra
grammar_rules.function_gloss: COM ('with, together with')
grammar_rules.description: Marks accompaniment or coordination.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: nee-ra ('with you'), Yoosefa-ra ('with Joseph')

grammar_rules.morpheme: -t- (-ti NOM, -ta ACC)
grammar_rules.function_gloss: PL (Plural Marker)
grammar_rules.description: Inserted before the case vowel: -ti for nominative plural and -ta for accusative plural.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: tamaare-ti (NOM.PL), tamaare-ta (ACC.PL)

grammar_rules.morpheme: Keena, Mala, Kanddo, Medheta, Dabbotetha Sunqqo
grammar_rules.function_gloss: Pre-nominal Modifiers
grammar_rules.description: Modifiers precede the head noun and express quantity (keena), color/appearance (mala), character (kanddo), shape/nature (medheta), or affiliation (dabbotetha).
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: daro asi (Keena), luulo mithi (Medheta), Goofa dere (Dabbotetha)

grammar_rules.morpheme: -iss- / -is- (CAUS), -ett- / -et- (PASS/REFL/RECIP)
grammar_rules.function_gloss: Active (Os-meqo), Passive (Ost-meqo) & Causative
grammar_rules.description: Valency-changing suffixes attached directly to the verb root before tense/aspect/person markers.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: tamaar-ss- ('teach'), xaaf-ett- ('be written'), pentt-iss- ('cause to boil')
grammar_rules.source: Sellassie Cheru (2015), Ch. 7; Gr. 10 Textbook, p. 86

grammar_rules.morpheme: Pinniyaa Peesho (Transitive) vs. Pinnonna Peesho (Intransitive)
grammar_rules.function_gloss: Direct Object Licensing
grammar_rules.description: Pinniyaa peeshota require a direct object (kaalodde) in the accusative case, whereas pinnonna peeshota take only a subject (yohaadde).
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: Na7ay qumaa mis (Pinniyaa) vs. Tami eexxees (Pinnonna)

grammar_rules.morpheme: -ays (1S), -aasa (2S), -ees/-is (3MS), -awsu/-asu (3FS), -oos/-ida (1PL), -eeta/-ideta (2PL), -oosona/-idosona (3PL)
grammar_rules.function_gloss: Ha7ode (PRES) & Aadhode (PAST) Paradigm
grammar_rules.description: Fused portmanteau suffixes encoding Tense/Aspect (Present/Imperfective vs. Past/Perfective), Person, Number, Gender, and Declarative Mood.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: ooth-ays ('I work'), ooth-ees ('he works'), ooth-is ('he worked'), ooth-idosona ('they worked')
grammar_rules.source: Sellassie Cheru (2015), Ch. 7; Gr. 8 Textbook, p. 22

grammar_rules.morpheme: -ana (Sinthode / FUT), -anaw / -ana-u / -anaas (INF / PURP)
grammar_rules.function_gloss: Future Tense & Purposive Infinitive
grammar_rules.description: Invariant future marker -ana across persons in declarative clauses; -anaw/-anaas marks purposive 'in order to'.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: yel-ana ('will give birth'), sabbak-anaw ('in order to preach')

grammar_rules.morpheme: -idi / -ada (CNV.ANT), -ishe / -ashe (CNV.SIM), -ikko (COND 'if')
grammar_rules.function_gloss: Medial Converbs & Conditional
grammar_rules.description: Chaining clauses in SOV narrative discourse: -idi (3MS/PL) / -ada (1S/2S/3FS) marks sequential actions ('having done...'); -ishe/-ashe marks simultaneous action ('while doing...').
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: dendd-idi ('having risen'), kaaleth-ishe ('while leading'), gakk-ikko ('if it arrives')

grammar_rules.morpheme: -enna / -ikke (PRES.NEG), -ibeenna / -abeenna (PAST.NEG), -oppa / -ofite (PROH)
grammar_rules.function_gloss: Negative Declarative & Prohibitive
grammar_rules.description: Negative suffixes attach to the verb stem to negate present, past, or imperative clauses.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: koy-ibeenna ('he did not want'), yayy-ofa ('do not fear!')

grammar_rules.morpheme: Wode, Besse, Keena, Hanota Peeqo / Suntha, Sunqqo, Peesho, Peeqo Tura
grammar_rules.function_gloss: Adverbial Subclasses & Head-Final Phrases
grammar_rules.description: Adverbs specify time (wode), place (besse), degree (keena), or manner (hanota). Phrases (tura) are head-final.
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: zine shammasu (Wode), karen uttis (Besse), loythidi oothees (Keena), woxxishe bis (Hanota)

grammar_rules.morpheme: nne ('and'), woykko ('or'), gidoppe attin / shin ('but/however'), hessa gisho ('therefore'), gujjidikka ('furthermore')
grammar_rules.function_gloss: Clause Coordination & Discourse Cohesion
grammar_rules.description: Conjunctions and discourse markers link clauses into cohesive paragraphs (daassa) and essays (adarso).
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: Otoroy loythi nabbabis; hessa gisho lo7o bessi gakkis.
grammar_rules.source: Grade 8 Textbook, p. 26; Grade 10 Textbook, p. 11

grammar_rules.morpheme: Gr8_Ch1_QAW_01: 1. Sunthi (Nouns & 7 Subclasses): Buzo sunthi (Proper: Baqul
grammar_rules.function_gloss: 1. Nouns (Sunthi) and 7 Subclasses: Proper (Buzo), Common (Kothe), Collective (Shiiqo), Abstract (Beettonabata), Materia
grammar_rules.description: 1. grammar_rules.example_gofatho: 1. Sunthi (Nouns & 7 Subclasses): Buzo sunthi (Proper: Baqulo, Zentto, Sawula), Kothe sunthi (Common: na7a, boori, tamaare), Shiiqo sunthi (Collective: dago, wude, dere asa), Beettonabata sunthi (Abstract: era, cincca, siiqo, ufayssa), Miishe sunthi (Material: saaxine, shuchchi, oyde, mithi), Taybettiya sunthi (Countable), Taybettonna sunthi (Uncountable: haathe, maathi, dhiille).

grammar_rules.description: Independent vs. Dependent Clauses (pp. 33–35): Independent clauses end in a finite verb (e.g., massis, pee7is, qopees), whereas dependent clauses end in converbs (-idi, -ada) or subordinators (gidida gisho). | Amharic: ንዑሳን ዓረፍተ ነገሮች (ገጽ 33–35)፦ (1) ራሱን ችሎ የሚቆም (ነጻ) ዓ.ነገር (Pana danda7idi eqqiya)፤ (2) ራሱን ችሎ የማይቆም (ጥገኛ) ዓ.ነገር (Pana danda7idi eqqonna)።

grammar_rules.morpheme: Gr9_Ch7_QAW_01: 1. Goofatho Doona Xaafo Hiillatanne Pidaleta Qaala Giddon Wo
grammar_rules.function_gloss: 1. Six Fundamental Gofatho Orthographic & Phonotactic Rules (Zara 5, pp. 63–65): Formalizes CV syllable templates (Ustta
grammar_rules.description: 1. Six Fundamental Gofatho Orthographic & Phonotactic Rules (Zara 5, pp. 63–65): Formalizes CV syllable templates (Ustta 'U' = Vowel, Guttuma 'G' = Consonant), bans initial consonant clusters/geminates (*GGUG) and initial vowel hiatus (*UUGU), mandates glottal stop '7' between medial vowels (sa7a, na7a, ma7o), and defines consonant gemination and vowel length. | Amharic: 1. የጎፋኛ ቋንቋ የፊደላት አጻጻፍ ሕግጋት (Ustta = አናባቢ፣ Guttuma = ተነባቢ፣ ገጽ 63–65)፦ (1) ሁለት የተለያዩ አናባቢዎች በቃል መነሻ ላይ አይደረቡም፤ (2) ተነባቢዎች በቃል መነሻ ላይ አይጠብቁም (*GGUG አይፈቀድም)፤ (3) ሁለት አናባቢዎች በቃል መካከል ሲገናኙ ግሎታል '7' ይገባል (sa7a, na7a, ma7o)፤ (4) ተነባቢዎች በቃል ውስጥ ሲደረቡ ጠብቀው ይነበባሉ፤ (5) አናባቢዎች ሲደረቡ ተስበው (ረዝመው) ይነበባሉ፤ (6) ጥምር ተነባቢዎች (ch, dh, dz, ph, sh, th, zh) አንድ ድምፅ ይወክላሉ።
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: 1. Goofatho Doona Xaafo Hiillatanne Pidaleta Qaala Giddon Wogara Xaafo Maara (6 Core Orthographic Rules & Zara 5 CV Table, pp. 63–65): Ustta = U (vowel), Guttuma = G (consonant). Rules: (1) Two different vowels (usttati) never cluster at word onset; (2) Consonants (guttumati) never geminate at word onset (*GGUG is illegal); (3) When two different vowels meet word-medially, glottal stop '7' (gilootaley) is inserted (e.g., sa7a, na7a, ma7o); (4) Doubled consonants medial-internally are pronounced geminated (minni nabbabettoosona); (5) Doubled vowels are pronounced long (aduqqi nabbabettoosona); (6) Digraph consonants (waatha guttumati: ch, dh, dz, ny, ph, sh, th, zh) represent a single phoneme. Zara 5 patterns: U (i, ee), GU (ba, ta, ne), GUGU (mata, kathi, qofa), GUGUGGU (timirtte, atarqqa), UGGUGUGU (asttamaare), GUGUU (nam77a, gam77a).
grammar_rules.source: Grade 9 Shemppo 7: Kovide-19 Kooroona Vayresse Hargge (pp. 54–64)

grammar_rules.description: The Five Parts of Speech in Gofatho (4.F Qawosa, pp. 35–38): Nouns (Sunthi), Verbs (Peesho), Adjectives (Sunqqo), Adverbs (Peeqo), and Function Words (Dabbotho: Postpositions 'Sigetho' and Conjunctions 'Gasetho'). | Amharic: አምስቱ የጎፋኛ የቃል ክፍሎች (4.F Qawosa፣ ገጽ 35–38)፦ (1) ስም (Sunthi)፣ (2) ግስ (Peesho)፣ (3) ቅጽል (Sunqqo)፣ (4) ተውሳከ ግስ (Peeqo)፣ (5) መስተዋድድና አያያዥ (Dabbotho፦ Sigethonne Gasetho)።

grammar_rules.function_gloss: 2. Transitive (Pinniyaa) vs. Intransitive (Pinnonna) Verbs (6.F Qawosa, pp. 60–61): Defines verbal valency and direct-ob
grammar_rules.description: 2. Transitive (Pinniyaa) vs. Intransitive (Pinnonna) Verbs (6.F Qawosa, pp. 60–61): Defines verbal valency and direct-object licensing in Gofatho. | Amharic: 2. ተሻጋሪ ግስ (Pinniyaa Peesho) እና ኢ-ተሻጋሪ ግስ (Pinnonna Peesho) (6.F Qawosa፣ ገጽ 60–61)፦ ተሻጋሪ ግስ ድርጊቱ ከባለቤት (Yohaadde) ወደ ተሳቢ (Kaalodde) የሚሻገርበት ነው (ምሳሌ፦ 'ድመቷ አይጧን ገደለች')፤ ኢ-ተሻጋሪ ግስ ደግሞ ተሳቢ አይፈልግም (ምሳሌ፦ 'እኛ ሳውላ እንኖራለን'፣ 'ፀሐይ በምሥራቅ ትወጣለች')።
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: 2. Pinniyaa Peesho (Transitive Verbs) vs. Pinnonna Peesho (Intransitive Verbs) (6.F Qawosa, pp. 60–61): Pinniyaa peesho transfers action from Yohaadde (Subject) to Kaalodde (Object): 'Gawariyaa eceriwu wodhasu' ('The cat killed the mouse'); 'Ta na7aawu kathaa ma' ('My child, eat the food'). Pinnonna peesho has no direct object: 'Nuuni Sawlan de7oos' ('We live in Sawla'); 'Awi dolohara keyees' ('The sun rises in the east'); 'Tami eexxees' ('The fire burns'). Ambivalent verbs (e.g., 'so77is' / 'feared').

grammar_rules.function_gloss: Active Voice (Os-meqo) and Passive Voice (Ost-meqo) Derivations (9.F Qawosa, pp. 86–87): Formalizes agentive passive ('-
grammar_rules.description: Active Voice (Os-meqo) and Passive Voice (Ost-meqo) Derivations (9.F Qawosa, pp. 86–87): Formalizes agentive passive ('-n' / '-ppe' on demoted agent + '-ett-' on verb) and agentless passive ('Muuzey tokettis'). | Amharic: የድርጊት (Os-meqo) እና የተደራጊ (Ost-meqo) ዓረፍተ ነገሮች (9.F Qawosa፣ ገጽ 86–87)፦ በድርጊት ዓ.ነገር፦ 'ቡናሮ ሙዝ ተከለ (Bunnaaroy muuze tokkis)'። ወደ ተደራጊ ሲቀየር፦ (1) 'ሙዙ በቡናሮ ተተከለ (Muuzey Bunnaaron/Bunnaaroppe tokettis)' ወይም (2) 'ሙዙ ተተከለ (Muuzey tokettis)'።
grammar_rules.example_gofatho: Os-meqonne Ost-meqo (Active Voice and Passive Voice, 9.F Qawosa, pp. 86–87, cited from Beddilu Wozza 2014): In Os-meqo (Active), the agent subject (Yohaadde) performs the action: 'Wozaakkoy keethe keexxis' ('Wozaakko built a house'); 'Bunnaaroy muuze tokkis' ('Bunnaaro planted a banana tree'). In Ost-meqo (Passive), the object (Kaalodde) takes nominative '-y', the agent optionally takes instrumental/locative '-n' or ablative '-ppe', and the verb takes passive '-ett-': (1) 'Muuzey Bunnaaron tokettis' or 'Muuzey Bunnaaroppe tokettis' ('The banana tree was planted by Bunnaaro'); (2) Agentless passive: 'Muuzey tokettis' ('The banana tree was planted').
